title: Plant a seedling: hold it upright in the hole with one hand while tipping the soil in with the other, then let it stand
instruction: Plant the seedling in the middle of the planting hole, upright, with its root plug on the bottom of the hole; fill the hole with the soil from the tray up to the top of the plug all round; and leave the seedling standing on its own.
context: This is the familiar potting task of keeping a delicate transplant upright at its original depth while tipping growing medium into the narrow space around its root plug. The round-bottomed plug tips unsupported in the empty hole. The second hand must keep the plant centered while the fill passes around it and settles.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Positions are in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward (away from the arms), y to the robot's left. A fixed wooden potting bench, 5 cm tall, covers x 16 to 44 and y -20 to 16, with a square planting hole 8 x 8 cm and 4.5 cm deep in it, centred at x 32, y 3 (x 28 to 36, y -1 to 7); the hole's rim is the bench top. A seedling (80 g) stands in a fixed black nursery cell (4.4 x 4.4 cm inside, 4.5 cm deep) on the bench at x 24, y 8: its root plug is 4 cm across and 4.5 cm tall, as tall as the hole is deep, with a round bottom; its stem is 0.8 cm square and reaches 15 cm; three leaves 5 cm long cross at its top. Because the plug's bottom is round, the seedling falls over when it is neither held nor surrounded by soil. A blue plastic tray (80 g; 9 cm wide, 13 cm deep, 3.5 cm walls, open at the front, with ribs 1 mm high across its floor and a flat handle 2 x 4 x 1.2 cm sticking back out of the top of its back wall) lies on the bench to the right of the hole (x 27.5 to 36.5, y -14.3 to -1.3), its open front 3 mm short of the hole's right edge. In it are 140 soil crumbs, balls 1.2 cm across of 1.1 g (153 g in all), in four layers at its back. The 288 mL hole takes about 240 mL around the 48 mL plug. The simulated crumbs have 127 mL of solid volume and settle with gaps. For the physical reset use 275 ± 5 mL of loose screened expanded-clay medium. Follow the README for the seedling, volume and fixture checks. The seedling, the tray and the crumbs are loose; the bench and the cell are fixed. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: The bodies' poses and speeds are read from the simulation, and each gripper's centre from the arm's joints. The soil level is measured at four spots 1 cm in from the middle of each side of the hole (in front of, behind, left and right of the plug), as the height at which a flat-ended rod 1 cm across, set down on the soil there, rests; in the simulation, the top of the highest crumb under the rod's end, counting only crumbs lying still (under 5 cm/s) in the hole, not in the tray and 3 cm or more from both grippers. The seedling is planted when it stands upright (within 10 degrees), its plug's axis within 1 cm of the hole's centre and its bottom within 5 mm of the hole's floor. Partial credit is the best stage reached during the run, held or not: 0.25 planted with the soil at all four spots at least halfway up the hole (2.25 cm above its floor); 0.5 planted with the soil at all four spots at most 1 cm below the rim and at most 1.5 cm of soil on the plug's top (measured 1.2 cm from the stem, in front, behind, left and right). 1.0: that, with both grippers' centres 8 cm or more from the seedling's axis and the seedling still (moved less than 1.5 mm and turned less than 1 degree over 1 s), for 1 s. The number of crumbs in the hole earns nothing by itself. Doing nothing scores 0. In a real trial: lay a straightedge across the rim and, at the four marked spots, set a 1 cm dowel down on the soil and measure with a ruler how far below the straightedge it rests; use the same dowel at four spots 12 mm from the stem and compare to the plug-crown height marked on the stem; measure lean with a protractor and check placement and release from overhead and scaled side video. Before the pour, use the crown height and measured plug height and tilt to verify the plug's floor clearance.
reset_notes: Empty the hole and return the tray and coherent rooted plug to the taped starting positions. Measure 275 ± 5 mL of rinsed, dry Plagron Euro Pebbles screened to 10–14 mm. Pour into the rear of the tray without shaking and leave the first 20 mm at the open lip clear. Use the same substrate batch and replace any damaged seedling. A physical trial needs the fixture and plug checks in README.md. The simulation resets its 140 particles to the exact listed positions.
fidelity: Isaac Sim 6.1 rigid bodies at 20 Hz. The soil is 140 rigid spheres 12 mm across with friction 0.3 and rolling damping. At four points the scorer computes where a 10 mm dowel first contacts the settled particles. Ribs 1 mm high hold the particles until tray tilt. The seedling is one rigid body with a round-bottom plug, stem and three leaves. The repeatable physical backfill uses screened expanded clay. Soil compaction and stem bending are outside the simulation.
scores: Scripted demonstration reached 1.0 in 488 steps. Dream-1 scored 0.0 in 2,400 steps. The one-sided pour and 45-particle charge controls scored 0.0 in 560 and 540 steps, respectively.
